title: a proof that patches a name the judge it asks reads in another process is reported, naming the patched target
intention: build_inspector reports a proof that patches a module attribute in its own process while a judge it asks (directly, through an ask alias, through a transitions function that reaches the wire, or through one proof-local helper) runs in another process and reads that attribute: the report names the proof, the patched target, the judge and the reach chain; a target it cannot resolve is listed, never dropped.
why: Measured 2026-11-14, three cases of one class: judges answer in CodeMother's process since 17d570c10390, so a patch made in the asker never reaches the judge. corrosion's tooth 2 (citation.ruling_covers_path, 149b), 3e08102ef35a's _TICKETS patches in test_transitions, test_entry_gate_jurisdiction and test_the_stones_are_pushed, and d3248e7cb2fd's crossings.ROOTS patch each went red long after the move and were found by hand. akiendell's scan over main plus the import_sieve fix flags 11 files / 91 findings, six of them new.
traces_to: Law 4 (a defect class found three times by hand needs an instrument); Law 3 (the report shows the patch is answer-side rather than assuming it); Law 8 (a peer leans on a green a patched asker manufactures).
how: A new module unseen_patches.py in the build_inspector machine (beside run_record.py, not inspector.py): unseen_patches(source, repo_root) walks a proof's ast for patch sites live across an ask-capable call, resolves the target through the proof's imports, and reports it only when import_sieve.reaches of the judge's module holds a file that reads the attribute; unseen_patch_proofs(repo_root) runs it over every proof. The judges are build_inspector's own: a judge name is a top-level function of inspector.py or run_record.py, read by ast from its own machine, so codemother's shim is not read. Not wired into lacks() or a sieve.

clauses.claim: a scratch proof in each of five positive spellings (with-patch, assignment, patch.object, an ask alias, a proof-local helper) is reported by unseen_patches, naming the patched target, the judge and the reach chain

seven asker-side negatives are silent (a module the judge does not reach, no ask in scope, an attribute no reached file reads, patch.dict(os.environ), a signature fake, a patch of the seam iw.ask, a judge that reads nothing patched) and an unresolvable target is listed as unresolved

over the real tree, the pre-fix sources at d41cdc76c of corrosion's tooth, test_transitions and test_entry_gate_jurisdiction are reported; the 0c2c draining fake at d41cdc76c is not, and six asker-side proof files are silent

decisions.text: D1: cairn/machines/build_inspector/unseen_patches.py reads patch sites, ask-capable calls (a literal ask of a judge, the judge being a top-level function of build_inspector's inspector.py or run_record.py read by ast; transitions' wire-reaching functions by its own ast call graph; one level of proof-local helper) and the answer-side reach through import_sieve.reaches. It lives in a machine because a tool calls no other Cairn component (outline 1.3.1; open-1ff5b870cb04 answered strict) and this one uses import_sieve; it reads its own machine's judges, never cairn/devices/codemother/shim.py (open-71c6ce696ed7).
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause, each calling unseen_patches over a scratch repo, never the build_inspector nest; it is not wired into lacks() or into a sieve.

out: cairn/tools/proof_coverage/ (a tool may not use import_sieve, outline 1.3.1)
wiring into lacks() or a sieve
fixing the flagged proofs (their own tickets)

measured.saw: corrosion tooth 2, 3e08's three _TICKETS proofs and d3248's ROOTS tooth patched names the remote judge reads; each found by hand
unseen_patch_proofs over origin/main plus bd008e7e9084 flags 11 files / 91 findings; 3/3 teeth green on Windows; a report-nothing stub red 3/3, a report-everything stub red on teeth 2 and 3
